liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Loose Lucy** (2 reviews): A friend claimed the band always played Loose Lucy when he saw them; it was played here; A friend remarked that Loose Lucy turned up at every Dead show he attended [11][17]
- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): Reviewer especially likes the first-set Cold Rain and They Love Each Other [8]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet>Fire feels rushed, though that is typical of 1991 [9]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The Wheel, arising out of Black Peter, is the second-set highlight, with an understated, even tone [13]

## The recordings

- **gd91-12-27.schoeps.oconnor.12094.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 185 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd91-12-27.sbd.hinko.25944.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sound and mix described as pretty good; Soundboard sound described as superb; Soundboard has some small quirks; not pristine [9][10][13][18]
- **gd1991-12-27.151628.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 172 min [5]
- **gd1991-12-27.144615.sbd.ultramatrox.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 20 songs; 183 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer bought tickets from scalpers in the parking lot and arrived around halfway through Cold Rain and Snow [11]
- Weather was bad in the lot; a stranger handed the reviewer a free ticket wishing her Merry Christmas [12]
- Heavy rain soaked the parking lot; Jerry walked slowly across the stage from left to right before tuning [16]
- Rainy parking lot; reviewer arrived late, while Cold Rain and Snow was playing [17]
- Taper felt these shows were a letdown after Bill Graham's death in a helicopter accident a few months earlier [7]
- Band's sound during this December run was lighter than the rest of 1991; Vince seemed to grow more confident each night [8]
- Called a warmup show by some; weaker than the following two nights but somewhat better than New Year's Eve [9]
- Smooth throughout, whereas the New Year's show was choppy and edgy [10]
- Did not measure up to the Halloween 1991 shows, but was a clean, standard performance [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd91-12-27.schoeps.oconnor.12094.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD(Schoeps)> DAT> CDR [1]. Also: Audience recording with Schoeps MK4 mics, to DAT, then CDR; via Billy DeLyon, seeded to etree by eD [1]
- **gd91-12-27.sbd.hinko.25944.sbeok.shnf**: source: DSBD > DAT > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [2]
- **gd1991-12-27.151628.sbd.cm.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  October 31, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [5]. Also: Soundboard recorded by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; multiple masters combined to complete the show; 24-bit converted to 16-bit at 44.1 [5]
- **gd1991-12-27.144615.sbd.ultramatrox.miller.flac1644**: taped by David Gans; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Dat Master (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Arena - December 27, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/december-27-1991) [21]
